title: Symmetry Preservation in Quantum Measurement: A Frame-Independent Postulate for Local Branch Selection
content: The textbook projection postulate of quantum mechanics stands in tension with the symmetries of relativistic spacetime: it is stated as an update applied at a single instant to the entire composite state, which presupposes a preferred simultaneity surface, and its description of the distant partner of an entangled pair invites the reading that measurement physically changes that partner. We argue that this tension arises from one removable ingredient of the axiom, and we make precise what that ingredient is and is not. Separating the postulate into three logically independent claims—definite-outcome realization, Born-rule probability, and a globally-timed projection—we show that the third can be replaced by a locally triggered rule: branch selection upon completed local decoherence, in the einselected pointer basis (Postulate M). The measurement operator itself is not modified: the update at a site A is of the local form PiA⊗IB under both the standard postulate and Postulate M, and the two rules yield identical post-measurement states and probabilities, the standard rule being recovered as the vanishing-decoherence-time limit. Postulate M is therefore a reinterpretation of standard quantum mechanics rather than a modification of it; what it changes is the trigger of the update, from a global instant to a local decoherence event, so that the axiom can be stated without reference to any foliation. Parameter independence holds exactly, as it does in the standard theory; the final branch structure and joint outcome statistics are foliation-independent; and the exchange symmetry of the entangled pair is respected. We illustrate the framework in the Einstein–Podolsky–Rosen (EPR) scenario with one and with both particles coupled to local spin environments. The Born-rule probabilities in the pointer basis are exactly conserved throughout decoherence, while the maximal CHSH (Clauser–Horne–Shimony–Holt) value, obtained from the Horodecki criterion, is Smax=2\( \sqrt{1+|z(t)|^2 } \) in terms of the decoherence factor z(t), interpolating between the Tsirelson bound and the classical bound; this corrects the constant-\( 2\sqrt{2} \) claim of Ref. [10]. The single symmetry that quantum mechanics does break, outcome independence, is located entirely in the nonseparability of the global state, never in the measurement operator: it transmits no signal and selects no frame. The single-outcome question—which branch is realized—is left open.
